events.what_changed: The fee-exemption paragraph was rewritten to add cross-border Indigenous persons and a 50% reduction for seasonal agricultural workers. Minors remain exempt, so the child-protection content is unaffected. In force on publication (Alcance 147, La Gaceta 158, 28 Aug. 2024).
events.passage: Quedarán exentos de estos pagos, las personas menores de edad, refugiadas, asiladas, apátridas, las personas mayores de edad con discapacidad, los trabajadores transfronterizos, las personas indígenas transfronterizas, así como turistas. [...] (Así reformado el párrafo anterior por el artículo 1° de la ley N° 10493 del 5 de junio del 2024)

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: unaccompanied and in-transit migrant children were channelled through PANI. In April–May 2023 PANI and DGME, with UNICEF, opened the two first temporary safe spaces in the Greater Metropolitan Area, bringing the total for in-transit migrant children to five (Ciudad Neily, Los Chiles, San José). This is evidence of the child-specific route working, but it covers only part of very large transit flows. 2026: the same PANI route continued, but in Feb. 2025 about 80 children deported from the US were held with their families at the CATEM-Sur in conditions HRW found unsuitable for children and without real access to asylum. The Sala Constitucional (Voto 2025-019485) ordered their release. That is a serious documented breach, but it is a single episode, not evidence of a systemic shift, so I keep the rating at Sometimes; Usually on both dates.

answers.notes: Two amendments in the window touch the cited instruments without touching the indicator. Ley 7739 art. 16 (permits for minors to leave the country) was reformed by Ley 10558 of 23 Oct. 2024; it is not cited and concerns all minors. Ley 8764 art. 6 gained an inciso 8 (students and researchers) through Ley 10645 of 24 Feb. 2025; inciso 7 is untouched. I did not read Voto 2025-019485 myself and use it only as practice evidence, via HRW and the starting coder. The 2023 rating rests on one UNICEF/PANI source, which is thin.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: the CEDAW Committee's concluding observations of March 2023 (CEDAW/C/CRI/CO/8) flagged barriers to justice for migrant, refugee and asylum-seeking women and limited information about remedies. In the February 2023 dialogue the State itself acknowledged greater inequality for migrant women. The framework operated, with known gaps. 2026: the Defensoría and MNPT reports in Voto 2025-019485, as relied on by the starting coder, found INAMU absent where deported women were held. Gender-based-violence services for displaced women (UNHCR partners, IOM-INAMU mapping) continued. The pattern is the same on both dates, so the rating stays at Sometimes; Usually.

events.instrument: Ley N.º 10493, Reforma del penúltimo párrafo del artículo 33; del primer párrafo del artículo 241, y del artículo 253, de la Ley 8764
events.what_changed: The exemption list was rewritten to add cross-border Indigenous persons and a 50% reduction for seasonal agricultural workers. The exemption for adults with disabilities appears in the new text and was already in force before through Reglamento art. 43, which has no amendment note. The disability protection is therefore unchanged in substance.

[...] (Así reformado el párrafo anterior por el artículo 1° de la ley N° 10493 del 5 de junio del 2024)

answers.implementation_then_now: I found no practice evidence specific to migrants with disabilities for either date. The 2026 rating rests on the starting coder's sources: DGME's own account of preferential handling of asylum seekers with disabilities (Expediente Público 2026), and coordination gaps at CATEM noted by the Defensoría and MNPT. I found nothing for 2022–2023 and no documented shift. The rating stays at Usually on both dates, inferred from the absence of documented breach for the fee exemption and dependant rules, with low confidence.

practice_sources.title: Human Rights Watch, Costa Rica: Allow Deported Migrants to Seek Asylum (no disability-specific finding)

answers.sourcing_note: The Refugee and Immigration Regulation provisions show no amendment notes in SINALEVI. For art. 33 of Ley 8764, I read the current text with its note and the text of Ley 10493 (via a law-firm reproduction; the Gaceta facsimile link redirected). I could not open the pre-2024 SINALEVI version, so the presence of the disability exemption on 1 Jan. 2023 is reconstructed from the unamended Reglamento art. 43 and the bill's stated purpose (agricultural workers' fees).
